## Objective
Build the playable browser front end for Snake: an HTML page with a canvas board, score display, start/pause/game-over overlay, keyboard controls and a game loop, all driven by the pure rules module `src/game.js` (global `SnakeGame`, being implemented in parallel by task T2). Opening `index.html` directly in a browser (a `file://` URL) must run the game with no build step, no server and no network.

## Interface
Files to create:
- `index.html`: HTML5 page, `<title>Snake</title>`, viewport meta tag, links `style.css`. Required elements, each with a double-quoted `id` attribute: canvas `board`; text spans `score` and `best`; overlay container `overlay` containing `overlay-title` and `overlay-hint` elements. At the end of `<body>`, two classic scripts in this order and with these exact relative paths: `<script src="src/game.js"></script>` then `<script src="src/main.js"></script>`. No `type="module"`, no `defer` needed.
- `style.css`: dark theme, board centred on the page, overlay absolutely positioned over the canvas with a translucent background and centred text, `.overlay[hidden] { display: none; }` equivalent so the `hidden` attribute hides it, canvas never wider than the viewport.
- `src/main.js`: classic script wrapped in an IIFE (no globals leaked, no `import`/`require`). It uses the global `SnakeGame` with exactly these members (see the contract in `src/game.js`): `createGame(cols, rows)`, `setDirection(state, direction)`, `step(state)`, `tickInterval(score)`. It looks up each of the ids listed above with a call of the form `document.getElementById('board')` (single-quoted id string).
- `README.md`: what the project is, how to run it (open `index.html` in a browser, or `python3 -m http.server` and visit the printed address), the controls, the rules (speed increases as you eat), how to run the rules tests (`node --test test/game.test.js`), and a short file map (`index.html`, `style.css`, `src/game.js` rules, `src/main.js` UI, `test/game.test.js`).

Constants at the top of `src/main.js`: `COLS = 20`, `ROWS = 20`, `CELL = 24` (pixels), a colour table (background, grid line, snake body, snake head, crashed head, food), and `BEST_KEY = 'snake.best'`.

## Behavior
1. Startup: create a game with `SnakeGame.createGame(COLS, ROWS)`, set the canvas pixel size to `COLS * CELL` by `ROWS * CELL`, draw the first frame, show the overlay with title `Snake` and hint `Press an arrow key, WASD or Space to start`, show score 0 and the stored best score.
2. UI phases: `ready` (before the first input), `running`, `paused`, `ended`. The overlay is visible in every phase except `running`.
3. Turn keys: ArrowUp/W maps to `'up'`, ArrowDown/S to `'down'`, ArrowLeft/A to `'left'`, ArrowRight/D to `'right'` (letters case-insensitive, matched on `event.key`). In `ready` a turn key starts the game (phase becomes `running`) and is also passed to `SnakeGame.setDirection`; in `running` it is passed to `setDirection`; in `paused` and `ended` it is ignored.
4. Space: `ready` becomes `running`; `running` becomes `paused` (overlay title `Paused`, hint `Press Space to resume`); `paused` becomes `running`; `ended` starts a brand-new game that is immediately `running`. Pressing Space must be ignored when `event.repeat` is true.
5. Game loop: use `requestAnimationFrame` with a time accumulator. While `running`, once the elapsed time since the last step reaches `SnakeGame.tickInterval(state.score)` milliseconds, call `state = SnakeGame.step(state)` exactly once and redraw; never perform more than one step per animation frame (no catch-up bursts after the tab slept). Resuming from `paused` or starting resets the accumulator so the first step is a full interval away.
6. After every step update the score element. If `state.status` is `'over'` or `'won'`, the phase becomes `ended`, the best score is updated and persisted when the score beat it, and the overlay shows title `Game over` (or `You win!` for `'won'`), with hint `Score: N. Press Space to play again`.
7. Auto-pause: when the page becomes hidden (`visibilitychange` with `document.hidden`) or the window loses focus (`blur`) while `running`, switch to `paused` and show the paused overlay. It never auto-resumes.
8. Rendering on the canvas each frame: fill the background, draw faint grid lines, draw each snake segment as a slightly inset rounded or plain square in the body colour, the head (`state.snake[0]`) in the head colour (crashed head colour when `state.status` is `'over'`), and the food (if not null) as a filled circle centred in its cell. Draw from `state` only; do not keep a second copy of the snake.
9. Best score: read from `localStorage` under `BEST_KEY` at startup (invalid or missing means 0) and write it back only when beaten; every storage access is wrapped in `try/catch` and falls back to an in-memory value, because storage can throw under `file://` or in private mode.
10. Key events: call `event.preventDefault()` for the arrow keys and Space (so the page does not scroll). Ignore any key event with `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` or `altKey` set, without calling `preventDefault`.

## Invariants
- Game rules live only in `src/game.js`. `src/main.js` must not re-implement collision, growth, food placement or speed formulas; it only calls `SnakeGame` and renders `state`.
- `state` is treated as immutable: always reassign it from the return value of `step` or `setDirection`.
- Works from `file://`: classic scripts only, relative URLs without a leading slash, no external fonts, CDNs or images.
- No third-party libraries and no build tooling.

## Edge cases
- `localStorage` throws or holds a non-numeric value: behave as if the best score is 0 and keep playing.
- Holding a key down fires repeated `keydown` events: turn keys may repeat harmlessly (the rules module caps its queue), Space must not.
- The tab is hidden mid-game: no step may run while hidden, and the game is paused when the tab returns.

## Guardrails
- Create only the four listed files. Do not touch `src/game.js` (owned by T2) or `test/game.test.js` (owned by T1).
- Do not add `package.json`, bundlers, TypeScript or test files for the UI.
- Do not write a `"type": "module"` anywhere; `src/game.js` is a classic script and CommonJS module.
- Element ids in `index.html` must use double quotes, and every id looked up in `src/main.js` must exist in `index.html` (the verify step cross-checks them).
- `src/game.js` is currently a stub whose functions throw `not implemented`; that is expected. Code against its documented contract, do not try to run the game here.

## Out of scope
Touch or swipe controls, sound, wrap-around walls, difficulty or board-size menus, devicePixelRatio scaling, animations between ticks, and any change to the game rules.
